Ancient DNA study traces syphilis bacteria back 5,500 years

Category: Science

Researchers sequenced an ancient genome of Treponema pallidum from a 5,500-year-old human skeleton found in the Sabana de Bogotá region of Colombia, providing the oldest genetic evidence yet for the syphilis-causing bacterial group [2][7][4]. The finding suggests treponemal diseases have circulated in the Americas far earlier than many prior timelines, potentially reshaping debates about when and where syphilis and its relatives emerged [3][6][5]. Scientists say combining skeletal evidence, archaeology, and paleogenomics is helping clarify a long-murky disease history—an encouraging example of modern tools illuminating ancient health questions [8].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Did you know: Treponemal diseases are caused by closely related bacteria that can produce different clinical syndromes, which is why genetic evidence is especially useful for untangling their history [2][7].

Key Points

  • Disease family: Treponema pallidum includes subspecies linked to multiple treponemal diseases—syphilis alongside yaws and bejel—so the ancient genome informs a broader disease family tree, not just one STI [2][7].
  • Where it fits: The work draws on remains from the Sabana de Bogotá area, and the genome’s age pushes molecular evidence for this bacterial lineage thousands of years deeper into the past than many earlier genetic datasets could reach [2][4][1].
  • Method blend: Researchers emphasize that interpreting treponemal disease origins benefits from integrating archaeological context, skeletal observations, and ancient-DNA data rather than relying on any single line of evidence [8].
  • History debate: Several articles frame the result as potentially refining long-running arguments about syphilis’s geographic origins by adding early American genetic evidence for a related lineage [4][3][6].
  • Why it matters: By expanding the ancient genomic record, the study helps researchers evaluate how treponemal pathogens evolved alongside human populations over long timescales [7][3].

Perspectives

Study researchers (Science paper): They report recovering a 5,500-year-old Treponema pallidum genome from Colombian remains and present it as a key data point for treponematosis evolution over millennia.

Sources: Science

Science editors/commentary: They argue that resolving syphilis origins requires integrating archaeological, skeletal, and paleogenomic evidence rather than treating genetic or skeletal clues in isolation.

Sources: Science

Popular science coverage: Coverage highlights that the ancient genome could shift public-facing narratives about syphilis’s timeline and geography, while noting the finding speaks to ancestors/relatives of modern strains rather than proving direct continuity.

Sources: Scientific American

Technical Details

  • Ancient pathogen genomics: Researchers extract and sequence degraded microbial DNA from ancient remains to reconstruct genomes and compare them with modern strains, enabling evolutionary timelines that do not rely only on symptoms or written records [7][8].
  • Treponematosis: A cluster of human diseases caused by Treponema species/subspecies (including those responsible for syphilis and yaws); identifying where an ancient genome sits on this tree helps infer how different disease forms may have evolved [7][2].
  • Genome recovery: The advance reported is recovery of a Treponema pallidum genome from 5,500-year-old remains, which provides direct genetic evidence rather than indirect skeletal inference [2][7].

Scientific Significance

  • Scientific meaning: The main scientific value is a new, very old genomic datapoint for Treponema pallidum, extending the time depth of genetic evidence and allowing researchers to test and refine evolutionary scenarios for treponemal diseases [7][2][3].
  • Uncertainty and confidence: Sources note that one ancient genome can anchor minimum ages and relationships, but it cannot by itself settle every origin question; broader sampling across regions and time periods remains important for confidence [3][6][8].
  • Limitations and future work: Commentary calls for more ancient genomes paired with archaeological and skeletal context to disentangle closely related treponemal diseases and to map how lineages spread and diversified over time [8][7].

Historical Background

Syphilis became widely documented in Europe in the late 15th century, fueling centuries of debate over whether it was introduced from the Americas after transatlantic contact or was already present in the Old World [common]. Modern paleogenomics has increasingly been used to test such origin stories by directly sequencing pathogen DNA from ancient human remains, complementing older approaches that relied on bone lesions and historical texts [8]. The new 5,500-year-old genome adds an early, well-dated American data point to that expanding record [2][7].

Q&A

Q: Does this genome prove the individual had venereal syphilis specifically?

A: The reports describe the genome as Treponema pallidum (a group that includes agents of multiple treponemal diseases), so it informs the broader lineage but does not automatically identify a specific clinical syndrome without additional context [2][8].

Q: Why is skeletal evidence alone hard to interpret for treponemal disease?

A: Articles emphasize combining skeletal observations with archaeological context and paleogenomics because different conditions can create overlapping bone changes, and genetics can provide more specific lineage identification [8].

Q: What kind of new samples would strengthen the origin timeline debate most?

A: Commentary points to the value of additional well-dated remains from multiple regions and periods, paired with both skeletal assessment and ancient-DNA sequencing, to better map spread and diversification [8][6].

Swiss and French teams entangle atoms for multiparameter sensing

Category: Science

Researchers at the University of Basel and France’s Laboratoire Kastler Brossel report a quantum-metrology method that uses entangled atomic clouds as an array of sensors to estimate several physical parameters at once with improved precision [1][3][4]. The work addresses a practical hurdle: real-world devices often need to track multiple fields or gradients simultaneously rather than optimize for a single quantity [4]. If the approach scales, it could help future instruments—such as advanced clocks and field sensors—extract more information per measurement, potentially making precision sensing more efficient and informative [4][1].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Did you know: Single-parameter quantum metrology is considered well established, while joint multiparameter metrology remains a newer frontier [4].

Key Points

  • Sensor array setup: The study frames the experiment as an “array of entangled atomic sensors,” aiming to distribute entanglement across multiple sensing elements rather than treating the atoms as one lumped probe [4].
  • Beyond one parameter: The authors position the result within “joint multiparameter” quantum metrology, an extension beyond the better-established single-parameter paradigm used in state-of-the-art clocks and field sensors [4].
  • Popular framing: Coverage emphasizes that the same entanglement once famous for “spooky” correlations is now being engineered as a practical resource for ultra-precise sensing [2].
  • Measurement promise: Phys.org and SciTechDaily highlight that the entanglement-enabled strategy can improve precision while targeting several quantities simultaneously, a capability that could reduce the need for separate, sequential measurements [1][3].

Perspectives

University of Basel and Laboratoire Kastler Brossel researchers: They describe entangling atomic clouds to enable simultaneous estimation of multiple physical parameters with enhanced precision in a quantum-sensor array [1][4].

Sources: phys.org

Science (journal) paper framing: The paper emphasizes that multiparameter estimation is less mature than single-parameter quantum metrology and targets the challenge of jointly estimating more than one quantity in many-particle entangled systems [4].

Sources: Science

ScienceBlog popularization: The coverage focuses on the practical upside—turning quantum “spookiness” into a tool for ultra-precise sensors—rather than on the formal estimation-theory framing [2].

Sources: scienceblog.com

Technical Details

  • Quantum entanglement: A quantum correlation between particles that can link measurement outcomes more strongly than any classical model allows; metrology uses it to reduce measurement noise below classical limits [4][common].
  • Multiparameter estimation: A measurement strategy that infers more than one physical quantity from the same dataset, which can be more realistic for sensors that must track several fields or gradients simultaneously [4].
  • Atomic sensor arrays: Using multiple atomic “sensing elements” (here, entangled atomic clouds) to probe a system; entangling elements can, in principle, improve how efficiently the array extracts information [4][1].

Industry Impact

  • Precision instrumentation: If entangled multiparameter readouts mature, atomic-clock and field-sensor designers could reduce trade-offs between monitoring different quantities by extracting them in a coordinated measurement rather than separate runs [4].
  • Quantum sensing R&D: The result supports the broader shift from “proof-of-principle” entanglement toward engineered resources in sensing, which could influence how labs prioritize architectures that distribute entanglement across sensor networks [2][4].

Scientific Significance

  • Scientific meaning: The work demonstrates a route to move quantum metrology from single-target demonstrations toward joint estimation, potentially increasing the information extracted per experimental cycle in atomic sensing platforms [4][1].
  • Uncertainty and confidence: All sources characterize the result as a precision enhancement enabled by entanglement, but the provided materials do not include quantitative error bars, confidence intervals, or scaling results that would let readers compare performance across regimes [1][3][4].
  • Limitations and future work: Because the reports emphasize capability rather than deployment, a key next step is showing robustness and scalability of entangled sensor arrays under realistic noise and system complexity for multi-quantity sensing tasks [4].

Historical Background

Quantum entanglement emerged as a defining feature of quantum theory and later became a resource for quantum information science [common]. In quantum metrology, researchers have long explored entangled many-particle states to beat classical precision limits for tasks like timekeeping and field sensing, but most mature demonstrations have focused on optimizing one parameter at a time [4]. The new result builds on this trajectory by targeting joint (multiparameter) estimation, which better matches how practical sensors often operate [4].

Q&A

Q: What kinds of physical parameters do atomic sensors commonly target in practice?

A: Atomic metrology platforms often aim at time/frequency references (clocks) and at detecting fields, which the Science article notes as key applications for entangled many-particle states [4].

Q: Why can estimating multiple quantities at once be harder than estimating one?

A: Because measurement choices and quantum correlations can couple the precision limits of different parameters, making joint optimization nontrivial compared with a single-parameter target [4].

Q: Does this approach require the atomic clouds to be separated in space?

A: SciTechDaily highlights entangled atoms “separated in space,” consistent with the idea of an array of distinct sensing elements rather than a single co-located probe [3][4].

  • Sexual selection: An evolutionary process where traits spread because they increase mating success through mate choice or competition, and the study interprets attractiveness and intimidation ratings through this lens [2][4].

  • Diminishing returns: A pattern where increases in a trait yield smaller gains beyond a threshold; women’s attractiveness ratings rose with penis size only up to a point, after which further increases mattered less [2][4].

Scientific Significance

  • Scientific meaning: The study offers empirical evidence—via controlled, systematically varied stimuli—that both mate choice and rival assessment can be linked to genital size perceptions, supporting a dual-pressure account discussed in popular coverage [2][1].

Historical Background

Evolutionary biologists have long debated why human genital morphology differs from other primates, with hypotheses ranging from female choice to sperm competition and male-male rivalry [4]. Sexual selection theory, introduced by Charles Darwin, formalized the idea that traits can evolve because they increase mating success, even if they do not directly improve survival [common].

Q: Did participants rate only penis size, or whole-body traits too?

A: They rated figures that varied simultaneously in height, shoulder-to-hip ratio, and penis size, allowing the study to examine combined effects of multiple cues [2][4].

Q: What does the study mean by men feeling threatened in two ways?

A: Men rated how intimidating figures seemed both as potential fighting opponents and as sexual rivals, and larger sizes increased both kinds of perceived threat in the reported results [2].

President Trump sues JPMorgan and Dimon for $5bn

Category: Business

President Donald Trump filed a lawsuit seeking at least $5 billion against JPMorgan Chase and its CEO, Jamie Dimon, alleging the bank improperly terminated him and some of his businesses as customers after the Jan. 6 Capitol attack [1][3][5][7][8][12][9]. The suit says JPMorgan closed multiple accounts in early 2021 with limited notice and frames the decision as political discrimination that disrupted operations and access to banking services [5][8][7]. JPMorgan said the case lacks merit, setting up a high-profile legal fight that could shape how banks manage reputational risk and customer offboarding decisions [5][7][12].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Did you know: JPMorgan Chase is the largest U.S. bank by assets [3].

Key Points

  • Where it’s filed: The lawsuit was filed in Miami-Dade County court in Florida, according to coverage of the complaint [5].
  • Account timeline: Trump’s complaint says JPMorgan moved to close accounts in February 2021 and provided a 60-day notice period [5].
  • Blacklist claim: The lawsuit alleges JPMorgan placed Trump and certain businesses on a reputational “blacklist” that could hinder opening accounts elsewhere [5][8][11].
  • White House tensions: The filing comes amid broader friction between the White House and Wall Street, including President Trump’s push to cap credit-card interest rates at 10%—a policy relevant to large card issuers like JPMorgan [5][12].
  • Post–Jan. 6 context: Several outlets tie the bank’s decision to the period after the Jan. 6 Capitol riot, which the suit cites as the backdrop for the account closures [3][8][6].

Perspectives

President Trump (plaintiff): The lawsuit argues JPMorgan ended banking services for political reasons and harmed Trump and his businesses by forcing them to quickly find replacement banking relationships [1][5][8].

Sources: Financial Times

JPMorgan Chase: JPMorgan said it believes the lawsuit has no merit [5][7].

Sources: CBS News

Jamie Dimon (named defendant): The complaint says Trump tried to raise the issue directly with Dimon and was told he would look into it, but the lawsuit alleges no follow-up occurred [5].

Sources: Fortune

Critics of the suit’s framing: Some coverage characterizes the lawsuit as part of a broader political-pressure campaign against major financial institutions, rather than a routine customer-service dispute [6].

Sources: Quartz

Timeline

  • January 6, 2021: Capitol attack becomes backdrop for alleged offboarding decision [3][8].
  • February 2021: Suit alleges JPMorgan began closing accounts with 60-day notice [5].

Technical Details

  • Debanking: “Debanking” refers to a bank terminating a customer relationship and closing accounts; the complaint argues this happened to Trump and some of his businesses in 2021 [1][3][12].
  • Reputational risk: Large banks run reputational-risk controls that can restrict or end relationships seen as potentially damaging; the lawsuit alleges JPMorgan used an internal “blacklist” for this purpose [5][8].
  • Customer offboarding notice: The complaint says JPMorgan provided a finite window (60 days) before closing the relevant accounts, a detail that matters operationally for payroll, payments, and financing continuity [5].

Industry Impact

  • Compliance policies: The case spotlights how reputational and political-risk considerations can intersect with account-closure decisions, potentially influencing how banks document and justify offboarding in the future [8][12].
  • Retail credit products: Because the dispute unfolds alongside President Trump’s call to cap credit-card interest rates at 10%, the episode underscores how regulatory pressure and politics can become intertwined with large banks’ consumer-lending economics [5].
  • Business banking access: The claims about knock-on effects for opening accounts elsewhere could increase scrutiny of interbank risk-sharing tools and informal “do-not-bank” practices, if they exist [5][11].

Historical Background

The lawsuit centers on events following the Jan. 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol, which multiple outlets cite as the period after which JPMorgan allegedly ended Trump’s banking relationship [3][8][6]. Banks commonly “debank” or offboard customers for compliance, fraud, sanctions, or reputational-risk reasons, and the dispute highlights the tension between private risk management and claims of viewpoint-based discrimination [common].

Q&A

Q: What remedies besides damages could the court award?

A: Depending on the claims, courts can consider injunctive relief (orders to do or stop doing something) or declaratory judgments in addition to monetary damages, though specific options depend on the causes of action in the complaint [common].

Q: How do banks typically decide to end a customer relationship?

A: Banks generally weigh legal and compliance obligations (such as fraud and sanctions screening) alongside profitability and reputational risk, then follow internal offboarding procedures and customer-notification requirements [common].

Q: Could this affect how other banks handle politically exposed clients?

A: If litigation increases scrutiny of “debanking” decisions, banks may respond by tightening documentation and standardizing decision processes for high-profile or higher-risk customers [common].

Action Items

  • Review your bank’s account-closure terms: Check your deposit agreement for notice periods and reasons a bank can close accounts, and keep a backup banking relationship for operational resilience [common].
  • Diversify payment rails: If you run a business, set up secondary payment options (e.g., an additional bank account or processor) to reduce disruption risk if an account is closed [common].

item.content:encoded:
TikTok finalizes US joint venture to avoid ban

Category: Business

TikTok said it has finalized a deal to create a new U.S. unit backed by major American investors, a structure intended to keep the app operating in the United States and head off the threat of a nationwide ban [2][6]. Several outlets described the arrangement as a joint venture that shifts operational control to a U.S.-based investor group while leaving parts of TikTok’s broader business with parent ByteDance [1][10]. A White House official told CBS News the agreement was finalized with China, and noted a 2024 sell-or-ban law had taken effect but has not been enforced by President Trump [3]. For users and creators, the immediate upside is continuity while governance and data-security safeguards are designed to address U.S. concerns [2][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Did you know: The TikTok joint-venture safeguards are designed to cover CapCut and Lemon8 as well, not just TikTok itself [10].

Key Points

  • Ownership split: Business Insider reported ByteDance will hold roughly a 20% stake in the new U.S. venture, while Oracle, Silver Lake and Abu Dhabi-based MGX will each own 15%, with affiliates of existing ByteDance investors holding around 30% [10].
  • Leadership setup: TikTok said Adam Presser will lead the new venture, and the majority-American board includes TikTok CEO Shou Chew, according to Business Insider’s account of the announcement [10].
  • Scope of safeguards: TikTok said the joint-venture safeguards will also cover CapCut, Lemon8 and other apps and websites in the U.S., expanding the deal’s reach beyond the flagship TikTok app [10].
  • Hawk criticism: The Financial Times said the deal has been criticized by China hawks even as TikTok launched a U.S. joint venture with American investors, signaling continued political scrutiny [1].
  • Algorithm question: Firstpost said U.S. investors receive majority control under the deal, but reported uncertainty remains over who ultimately controls TikTok’s recommendation algorithm [7].

Perspectives

TikTok: TikTok framed the joint venture as a way to keep operating in the U.S. while adding safeguards that also apply to CapCut and Lemon8.

Sources: Business Insider

White House official: A White House official told CBS News the deal was finalized with China and pointed to the 2024 sell-or-ban law that has not been enforced by President Trump.

Sources: CBS News

US China hawks: China hawks criticized the structure even as TikTok set up the U.S. unit, reflecting ongoing national-security concerns.

Sources: Financial Times

American investors: Major American investors are backing the new U.S. unit, which PBS described as an American version of the app designed to avert a ban threat.

Sources: PBS NewsHour

Technical Details

  • Joint venture structure: Several outlets described the solution as a new U.S. joint venture that shifts aspects of operational control and governance to American investors to meet U.S. legal requirements [1][6][10].
  • Sell-or-ban compliance: Business Insider said ByteDance’s stake of just under about 20% meets the divestment requirement set by the 2024 sell-or-ban law targeting apps owned in countries the U.S. deems foreign adversaries [10].
  • Recommendation algorithm: Firstpost reported that control of the algorithm remains a key open question in assessing how much independence the U.S. entity will have [7].

Industry Impact

  • Digital advertising: By preventing an immediate U.S. shutdown, the deal preserves a major channel for brands and small businesses that buy TikTok ads and depend on continuity of audience access [2][6].
  • Creator economy: Business Insider said TikTok’s U.S. workers can "finally breathe a sigh of relief," signaling improved stability for employees and the broader creator-and-agency ecosystem built around the platform [10].
  • M&A playbook: The multi-investor structure involving Oracle, private equity and a sovereign-backed fund (MGX) may serve as a template for how geopolitically sensitive apps attempt to localize ownership while keeping global parent-company ties [10][1].
  • App portfolios: TikTok said safeguards cover CapCut and Lemon8 too, which could reduce regulatory overhang for adjacent consumer apps and their monetization plans in the U.S. [10].

Historical Background

U.S. scrutiny of TikTok has centered on national-security concerns tied to its Chinese ownership and culminated in a 2024 law requiring a sale or ban, which CBS News said went into effect but has not been enforced by President Trump [3]. Chicago Tribune and MarketWatch described the agreement as the endpoint of a multi-year legal and political fight over whether TikTok could keep operating in the U.S. [8][6].

Q&A

Q: Which investor group members are described as managing investors?

A: Business Insider reported Oracle, MGX and Silver Lake will serve as managing investors in the new U.S. venture [10].

Q: Who leads the new U.S. venture day to day?

A: Business Insider reported TikTok’s Adam Presser is leading the new venture [10].

Q: What parts of the company does ByteDance still control?

A: The Financial Times and Business Insider reported ByteDance keeps core business lines such as e-commerce and ads, even as the U.S. unit is set up [1][10].

Action Items

  • Advertisers: confirm account continuity plans: Ask your TikTok account representative whether campaigns will be served by the new U.S. entity and whether invoicing, data access or brand-safety settings change under the joint venture [6].
  • Creators: review connected apps and tools: If you use CapCut or Lemon8 alongside TikTok, check whether any U.S.-specific terms or account settings update as the safeguards roll out across TikTok’s U.S. app portfolio [10].
